comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removed &.bullet{margin-top:5px} while parent stays float-based, not flex. WHY: The 5px compensation for the floated bullet is lost on topic pages where order() is a no-op, shifting bullet badges up relative to title text.

hist.text: The claim rests on .extra-info-wrapper's parent staying float-based so order() is a no-op, but .extra-info-wrapper is rendered only by header-extra-info inside the header .contents (header.hbs:94), which this PR turns into a flex container (common/base/header.scss:16-18). The removed 5px bullet offset is replaced by flex align-items:center plus line-height:1.5 (topic.scss:30-32).

The float-based main topic title still retains its bullet margin at app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss:10-13. The removed margin belongs to the header, where the category renders below the heading (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/header-extra-info.hbs:13-15), and the PR changes both header alignment and line-height; removing that spacing does not establish the claimed alignment defect.

The comment's premise is that the parent of .extra-info-wrapper stays float-based so order() is a no-op. At head .extra-info-wrapper is rendered only by header-extra-info (header-extra-info.hbs:1), invoked inside the header's div.contents (header.hbs:2, :94), and this PR makes .contents a flex container with align-items:center (common/base/header.scss:15-18). So order(2) is not a no-op and the parent is not float-based; the removed 5px offset is replaced by flex centering plus line-height:1.5 (topic.scss:30-32). The #topic-title bullet margin is untouched (topic.scss:10-14). Since the stated fact is false, this is a hallucination, not merely an unproven defect.

I retain FP/none: the main topic title's floated bullet retains its 5px margin, while the removed margin affects the header category rendered below its heading with newly adjusted line-height. The reviewer's assertion that order(2) works is incorrect: header-extra-info retains Ember's default component wrapper, so .extra-info-wrapper is not a direct flex child of .contents. That ineffective order does not establish the claimed bullet alignment defect.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The anchor pattern Pattern.compile("]*>") matches any tag whose name begins with 'a', such as ,
, and , not just anchor tags. WHY: Non-anchor 'a' tags are treated as anchors, so the verifier can emit misleading "Didn't find anchor tag" errors, or silently strip a non-anchor tag before the HTML policy runs when English contains the same tag. HOW: Require a word boundary after the 'a', e.g., ]*)?>, so only , , and are matched.

hist.text: ANCHOR_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>") (VerifyMessageProperties.java:145) does match <abbr>, <address>, <area> etc. as anchors. No message properties at head contain such tags (git grep finds none), so this is a theoretical imprecision in a build-time verifier.

VerifyMessageProperties.java:145 matches tags such as <abbr>, and lines 154–155 remove them when identical tags appear in English. Because removal precedes policy validation at lines 88–92, these non-anchor tags bypass the allowed-element policy; this PR introduces the defect.

The regex is imprecise as stated: ANCHOR_PATTERN "</?a[^>]*>" (VerifyMessageProperties.java:145) also matches <abbr>, <area>, <audio>, and santizeAnchors strips such a tag before the policy runs (lines 88, 153-155). But it strips only a tag that is byte-identical to one in the English source, so a translation can only carry a tag the project's own English file already has, which is the exemption the method is designed to grant anchors. No message bundle at head contains such tags, and this is a build-time verifier, not a runtime sanitizer. Real but no practical effect: nit.

I retain TP: the newly introduced regex strips non-anchor tags before policy validation, producing incorrect validation results. English bundles are also verified against themselves, so an English value containing `<abbr>text</abbr>` passes despite `abbr` being excluded from the allowed elements. Matching the English source therefore does not eliminate the defect. The absence of affected tags in current bundles limits its incidence, but this is incorrect behavior for uncommon input, not a cosmetic nit.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Organizer subject uses attendees[0].name after nameless guests are added. WHY: New guests are created with name "" so the subject renders an empty or wrong booker name. HOW: Use the original booker/organizer name instead of attendees[0].

hist.text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 uses attendees[0].name and addGuests.handler.ts:85 creates guests with name "", but attendees[0] is the original booker: the new guests are appended by createMany after the existing attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:92-106), the same attendees[0] convention as OrganizerScheduledEmail. The empty name only appears if a new guest were first, which this code does not do.

New guests receive an empty name in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:83-89, and the updated attendees are fetched without ordering at lines 92-108, so the original booker is not guaranteed to remain first. packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26-29 directly interpolates attendees[0].name, allowing a nameless guest to produce a blank booker name in the subject.

Guests are created with name "" (addGuests.handler.ts:83-90) and appended to the existing booking via createMany (:92-106), so the original booker row, inserted earlier, is attendees[0] in practice. organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 follows the same attendees[0] convention as OrganizerScheduledEmail and the rest of cal.com's emails. The missing orderBy is a theoretical ordering guarantee shared by every booking email, not a defect this PR introduces. The comment's claim that adding nameless guests makes the subject render an empty name does not happen on the normal path.

I retain TP: createMany inserts rows; it does not guarantee their position in the subsequently fetched attendees relation. The new handler fetches attendees without orderBy and passes that ordering directly to the new template, which interpolates attendees[0].name even though added guests have empty names. Neither mapping nor formatCalEvent restores the original booker to index zero. Also, OrganizerScheduledEmail actually uses calEvent.title for its subject, so the cited precedent does not establish correctness.
